summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted with two weeks of dyspnea, orthopnea, productive cough, and pleuritic chest pain radiating to the left shoulder. Initial evaluation revealed a moderate to large pericardial effusion with signs of early tamponade, bilateral pleural effusions, and leukocytosis. She underwent pericardiocentesis, draining 640 cc of serosanguinous fluid, after which her symptoms improved. A CT scan with contrast was performed but led to an anaphylactic reaction, requiring epinephrine and close monitoring; she recovered fully. The pericardial fluid showed no malignancy or infection, and the etiology remained unclear. She was treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin and managed for acute on chronic diastolic heart failure with continued diuresis. Her shoulder pain, previously attributed to musculoskeletal causes, improved post-procedure. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid iodinated contrast, monitor weight, restart atorvastatin, discontinue potassium and valsartan temporarily, and follow up with primary care and cardiology.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
